lead: A wall footing, also called a strip footing, spreads a long wall load over soil. The wall sits on a reinforced concrete slab that projects on both sides. Its width comes from service load divided by safe bearing capacity. Its thickness comes from bending at the wall face and one-way shear at distance d from that face. Only a few universities teach this. You meet it under compound walls, load-bearing brick buildings and boundary walls, where a narrow strip is cheaper than many isolated pads.
prereq: You need: beam bending from Unit 2, shear from Unit 3, and one-way slab detailing from Unit 4.

blocks.text: A wall footing is a long reinforced concrete slab under a wall. The wall load P is in kN per metre length. The safe bearing capacity q_safe is in kN/m². Choose the width from service load: B = P / q_safe. Include footing self-weight; if it is not included, add about 10% to P. B is in metres. The wall thickness t_w is in metres. The slab projects a = (B − t_w)/2 on each side. This projection is the cantilever that bends the slab. A 230 mm wall on B = 1.2 m gives a = 0.485 m. The factored soil pressure is w_u = 1.5 P / B in kN/m². Use w_u for strength checks, never the service pressure. The maximum moment per metre length is at the wall face: M_u = w_u a² / 2. M_u is in kN·m per metre. The free edge has zero moment. For M20 concrete and Fe415 steel, the limiting depth is d_req = √(M_u × 10⁶ / (0.138 f_ck b)). Use b = 1000 mm. Adopt overall depth D with cover 50 mm and bar diameter φ: d = D − 50 − φ/2. Keep edge thickness at least 150 mm. Main bars run across the width; find A_st as for a singly reinforced beam (see Unit 2).

Check one-way shear at a section d from the wall face. The cantilever length beyond it is a − d. Then V_u = w_u (a − d) per metre. The shear stress is τ_v = V_u × 10³ / (1000 d), in N/mm². Compare with τ_c from IS 456 Table 19 at p_t = 100 A_st /(1000 d). If τ_v exceeds τ_c, increase D; shear reinforcement is not provided in footings. Distribution steel runs along the wall length. Provide 0.12% of the gross section: A_st,dist = 0.0012 × 1000 × D, in mm² per metre. For D = 200 mm, use 8 mm bars at 200 mm c/c. Cover is 50 mm on the soil face. Punching shear does not govern a long strip; see isolated footings for that check. A uniform 200 mm slab suits light walls.

figure.caption: The wall load fixes the width from bearing. The factored soil pressure fixes the moment. The adopted depth is 250 mm. Notice that the moment is taken at the wall face.

spec.title: Wall footing
spec.aria: Wall footing flow from 180 kN per metre wall load, to 1.2 m width with safe pressure 150 kN per square metre, to factored soil pressure 225 kN per square metre, to 26.5 kN·m per metre moment, to 250 mm depth.

examples.question: A 230 mm brick wall carries a service load of 180 kN per metre length; this value includes the footing self-weight. The safe bearing capacity of the soil is 150 kN/m². Design the width and thickness of a wall footing using M20 concrete and Fe415 steel. Take cover 50 mm.
steps: Service width: B = 180 / 150 = 1.20 m. Projection: a = (1.20 − 0.23) / 2 = 0.485 m.
Moment at wall face: M_u = 225 × 0.485² / 2 = 26.46 kN·m/m.
Adopt D = 250 mm and 10 mm bars: d = 250 − 50 − 5 = 195 mm.
Steel from beam formula: A_st = 392 mm²/m. Provide 10 mm @ 140 mm c/c = 561 mm²/m; p_t = 0.29%.

Shear at d from face: x = 0.485 − 0.195 = 0.290 m; V_u = 225 × 0.290 = 65.3 kN/m; τ_v = 65.3 × 10³/(1000 × 195) = 0.33 N/mm². τ_c ≈ 0.38 N/mm² for p_t = 0.29%. τ_v < τ_c, so no shear reinforcement is needed.
Distribution steel: 0.0012 × 1000 × 250 = 300 mm²/m. Provide 8 mm @ 160 mm c/c = 314 mm²/m.
examples.answer: Adopt B = 1.2 m and D = 250 mm; main 10 mm @ 140 mm c/c and distribution 8 mm @ 160 mm c/c, with no shear reinforcement.
examples.check:
import math
P=180.0
q=150.0
tw=0.23
fck=20.0
fy=415.0
cover=50.0
phi=10.0
B=P/q
a=(B-tw)/2
Pu=1.5*P
wu=Pu/B
Mu=wu*a*a/2
d_req=math.sqrt(Mu*1e6/(0.138*fck*1000))
D=250.0
d=D-cover-phi/2
term=1-4.6*Mu*1e6/(fck*1000*d*d)
Ast=(0.5*fck/fy)*(1-math.sqrt(term))*1000*d
Ast_prov=(math.pi/4*phi*phi)*1000/140
Ast_dist=(math.pi/4*8*8)*1000/160
Vu=wu*(a-d/1000)
tau_v=Vu*1000/(1000*d)
pt=100*Ast_prov/(1000*d)
tau_c=0.36+(pt-0.25)/0.25*(0.48-0.36)
print(f'{B:g}')
print(f'{D:g}')
print(f'{Ast_prov:.0f}')
print(f'{Ast_dist:.0f}')
print(f'{tau_v:.2f}')
print(f'{tau_c:.2f}')

traps: Using service soil pressure with a factored moment. Multiply the wall load by 1.5 first.

Taking the bending moment at the footing edge. The critical section is at the wall face, because that section carries the full projection a as its lever arm; at every section closer to the free edge the remaining projection, and hence the moment, is smaller.
Using overall depth D in place of effective depth d in bending and shear.
Confusing distribution steel along the wall with main steel across the width; they run at right angles.

quiz.q: What is another name for a wall footing?
Why is the bending moment largest at the wall face?
quiz.a: The full projection a acts as the lever arm there, and moment grows with the square of projection.

quiz.q: A wall carries 150 kN/m. Safe bearing capacity is 100 kN/m². Find B.
B = 1.2 m, wall thickness 0.23 m. Find projection a.
Why check one-way shear at d from the wall face, not at the face?
quiz.a: The load within a distance d of the wall face is carried straight into the wall by diagonal compression, so a diagonal tension crack cannot form there. A crack can start only at about d from the face, so IS 456 clause 34.2.4.1 makes the section at distance d the critical section for one-way shear.

quiz.q: A design uses service pressure 150 kN/m² with a factored moment. What is wrong?
quiz.a: Moment and pressure must use the same load level. Factored moment needs factored pressure, 225 kN/m², otherwise steel is underdesigned.

beyond: Not for the exam. In practice, wall footings are often reinforced strips under load-bearing masonry, or turned into strap footings when a boundary wall sits on the edge of a plot. Modern software models the soil as springs, so the pressure is not uniform. Geogrid reinforcement and lime stabilisation can raise the safe bearing capacity of weak soil. Search next for 'strap footing', 'eccentric wall footing' and 'IS 1904 bearing capacity'.
